• Explains the real clinical workflow and approved workarounds.
  • Validates requirements and workflow impact.
  • Represents department/site needs.
  • Helps communicate changes and training.
  • Identifies patient-safety or compliance concerns.

• Runs defined test cases in the appropriate environment.
  • Reproduces common and edge-case workflows.
  • Captures expected versus actual results without unnecessary PHI.
  • Confirms modality, worklist, PACS, and downstream behavior.
  • Provides clear go/no-go feedback within the test window.

• Full name, title, department, modality, primary site, and backup site.
  • Super-user, tester, trainer, approver, or backup role.
  • Applications and workflows they know: eCW, AbbaDox, Merge, MagView, modality console, reporting, or specialty tools.
  • Testing availability, preferred scheduling method, and backup contact.
  • Whether they can test normal workflow, corrections, downtime/recovery, interfaces, and patient-safety edge cases.
  • Who gives final clinical approval when tester feedback conflicts.

• Ask Craig: top three priorities, current projects, systems you will own vs support, urgent issue definitions, expected 30/90-day capabilities, and success measures.
  • Ask Amber: application-team responsibility split, change-control process, recurring pain points, departments, vendors, and production-documentation expectations.
  • Build the people map: application owners, infrastructure/network/storage/security owners, managers, on-call contacts, and RIS/PACS/breast/cardiology/scheduling super users.
  • Close access gaps: ticketing, VPN/remote support, PACS/RIS admin, eCW, MagView, AMICAS Watch, AbbaDox Wiki, interface monitoring, approved logs, documentation repositories, and vendor portals. Request least privilege; do not assume domain/SQL/virtualization admin is required.
  • Validate one exam end to end: registration/order → scheduling → MWL → acquisition → PACS → radiologist → report → eCW. Record owner, identifier, interface, success signal, failure checkpoint, and escalation at every step.
  • Use the modality visit: meet Dawn and technologists; capture vendor/model, modality, location, worklist source, PACS destination, common problems, manual steps, workarounds, and support ownership. Record IP/AE details only in an approved secure location.
  • Observe clinical work: radiology technologist, radiologist, scheduling/registration, breast center, and cardiology workflows. Ask what breaks, what is manual, and what is not documented.
  • End-of-week review: reconcile new facts into the wiki, list unanswered questions, identify access blockers, and agree on Week 2 priorities with Craig.

• HL7/interface map: identify engine, ADT/ORM/ORU/SIU or equivalent routes, eCW/AbbaDox/Merge/MagView/reporting endpoints, ACK behavior, failure queues, replay rules, alerts, owners, and test environment.
  • DICOM endpoint map: AE Titles, authorized IP/FQDN, ports, storage SCPs, MWL provider, Query/Retrieve, Storage Commitment if used, routing rules, relevant destinations, and who controls changes.
  • Merge operational baseline: normal queue depth/age, error mix, ingest volume, archive/restore latency, alert rates, study-state transitions, and approved evidence-gathering steps.
  • AbbaDox: obtain Wiki/admin documentation; validate statuses, Tech Complete actions, MWL, scheduling/intake ownership, interface monitoring, and support escalation.
  • MagView: confirm version, modules, servers/database, MagLink/MagTAC use, and ownership of BI-RADS, reporting, risk, tracking, recalls, lay letters, MQSA, and follow-up.
  • Reporting: identify dictation/speech-recognition and structured-reporting product, worklist integration, preliminary/final/addendum flow, critical results, report correction, and result delivery.
  • Support model: document clinical user → applications → infrastructure/network → vendor/modality engineer path and which patient-impact events bypass normal escalation.

• Server/infrastructure inventory: application/database/interface hosts, virtual/cloud platform, service assignments, storage, network dependencies, DNS, certificates, service accounts, file shares, patching, and vendor access.
  • Archive/backup/DR: HSM product, storage tiers, free capacity/growth, retention, second copy, replication, RPO/RTO, restore ownership, downtime procedures, and last successful recovery test.
  • Downtime runbooks: PACS, RIS, HL7/interface, network, modality, reporting, and breast workflow; confirm who declares downtime and how clinical operations continue and reconcile afterward.
  • Common-incident playbooks: missing images/exam/MWL, wrong patient/accession/demographics, duplicate study, stuck Unverified, missing radiologist worklist item, report not in eCW, failed routing, interface backlog, slow viewer, outside-image import, and prior restore.
  • Vendor and support matrix: product, account/customer number location, support portal/phone, severity rules, after-hours escalation, contract/renewal owner, and internal approval path.
  • Security and audit: provisioning/deprovisioning, privileged access, audit logs, encryption, remote access, break-glass procedures, and who can perform high-risk PACS corrections.
  • Operational risks: produce a prioritized top-10 list using patient impact, likelihood, detectability, recovery readiness, unsupported versions, single points of failure, capacity, and documentation gaps.
  • 30-day review: present the current topology, confirmed facts, unresolved risks, access gaps, quick wins, and proposed next-month priorities to Craig.

• Is the study eligible under Qualifier rules?
  • Was an archive job created?
  • Did Archiver process it?
  • Did HSM accept and protect the objects?
  • Can PACS restore the study within the clinical SLA?

• Confirm correct worklist selection, accession, send time, source AE/IP, and modality send status.
  • Check Listener/Importer health and Image Import/Insert File queues.
  • Search for association, rejection, unsupported object/transfer syntax, DB, storage, timeout, and identity errors.
  • Check for partial series or a duplicate study under different identifiers.

• Check Unverified, Unread, In Use, Priority, completed/final, filters, assignment, and permissions.
  • Validate import completion, expected series, order/accession match, location, modality, and subspecialty.
  • Do not force Unverified → Unread before understanding why the state exists.

• Record monitor, metric, threshold, time window, value, duration, node, and linked log.
  • Identify what increments and clears the counter and whether users have symptoms.
  • Red threshold status may represent elevated workflow activity—not necessarily an outage.
